title: Review: post-KITH-1tsc audit (attach, events, tslocal, kithd periphery)
notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — Two P1 security issues (XSS via ?accept= + unenforced body size limit) and two architectural gaps (unconditional HTTP fallback + SSRF guard scope) that would generate CVE-class reports from a public GitHub audience. The web client is clean (textContent throughout, no client-side secret storage), the auth model is solid, and WhoIs is correctly fail-closed. The attach/blob layer and kithctl peripheral modules were not previously reviewed and contained the bulk of this round's findings.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: (1) discovery.rs contact auto-upsert behavior not filed — may be intentional design, needs owner decision; (2) kithd/src/events.rs and kithd/src/tls.rs peer_fetch certificate verification path not fully read; (3) group chat paths in kithd not re-reviewed this cycle. Would raise confidence if: discovery auto-upsert behavior is explicitly documented as intentional or restricted to approved contacts; /jmap/events owner-check enforcement is confirmed; group_and_receipt.rs e2e tests read.
